1: ## 1. Plugin and config 2: 3: - [x] 1.1 Add `gem "jekyll-polyglot"` to the `:jekyll_plugins` group in `Gemfile`. 4: - [x] 1.2 Run `bundle install` locally and confirm `jekyll-polyglot` is resolved and `Gemfile.lock` is updated. 5: - [x] 1.3 In `_config.yml`, add `languages: ["es", "en", "pt_BR"]` and `default_lang: es` at the top level (next to the existing `title`, `url`, `lang` keys). 6: - [x] 1.4 In `_config.yml`, add `exclude_from_localization:` with the list from design D1 (`assets/`, `search.json`, `feed.xml`, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `OneSignalSDKWorker.js`, `onesignal/`, `raw/`, `llms.txt`, `mcp.json`). 7: - [x] 1.5 Confirm a local `bundle exec jekyll build` still succeeds and `_site/` structure is unchanged on the default Spanish build (verify `_site/index.html` and `_site/categoria/` exist and no `/en/` or `/pt_BR/` directories appear yet — they will appear once posts carry `lang:`). 8: 9: ## 2. i18n data file and helper 10: 11: - [x] 2.1 Create `_data/i18n.yml` with three top-level keys (`es`, `en`, `pt_BR`). Mirror the structure shown in design D3, covering at minimum: `menu.recent_posts`, `menu.lang_label`, `footer.copyright`, `footer.tagline`, `topbar.archive`, `topbar.feed`, `topbar.menu`, `a11y.menu_open`, `a11y.menu_close`, `category_list.count_suffix`. 12: - [x] 2.2 Apply the **technical-terms rule** (design D10) when filling the dictionary: terms like `post`, `posts`, `feed`, `slug`, `permalink`, `archive`, `category`, `tag`, `loading` are byte-identical across `es` / `en` / `pt_BR`. Only natural-language labels (button copy, accessibility labels, prose taglines) get localized. 13: - [x] 2.3 Translate every natural-language key into the three languages. Spanish values match today's hardcoded strings exactly. pt_BR values are natural pt_BR (NOT PT-PT). English values are concise terminal-style. The `posts` token in `category_list.count_suffix` and the `recent_posts` identifier in `menu.recent_posts` are NOT translated. 14: - [x] 2.4 Create `_includes/i18n_string.html` with the Liquid logic from design D3 (read `include.key`, split on `.`, look up under `site.data.i18n[page.lang | default: site.lang]`, fall back to `site.lang` when the key is missing). 15: - [x] 2.5 Create a quick smoke check: build the site, then on a Spanish post confirm the include renders the Spanish value of `menu.recent_posts` (will be wired up in tasks 6/7 — for now just confirm `_includes/i18n_string.html` exists and the YAML parses). 16: 17: ## 3. Language selector partial and styles 18: 19: - [x] 3.1 Create `_includes/lang-selector.html`. Iterate the languages from `site.languages` (in their declared order) and emit the markup from design D4 for each. Use `i18n_string.html` for the `lang_label`. Mark the active row with `data-active="true"` when the row's `lang` matches `page.lang | default: site.lang`. 20: - [x] 3.2 For each row, build the `href`: look up the post that has the same `page_id` as the current page (and the target language) via `page.permalink_lang`, and emit its URL through the polyglot `static_href` block tag so the URL is not relativized. If no such translation exists, fall back to `/`, `/en/`, or `/pt_BR/` respectively based on the target language. 21: - [x] 3.3 Create `_sass/_lang-selector.scss` with the styling described in design D11: font `$font-mono`, base color `$ink-soft`, active row color `$accent-bright` under `[data-active="true"]`, hover lift to `$accent`, `:focus-visible` outline `1px solid $accent` with `2px` offset, a 1px `$rule-strong` bottom border separating the selector from the next block. 22: - [x] 3.4 Import the new partial in `assets/css/main.scss` (locate the existing `@use` block for overlay/topbar partials and add `@use 'lang-selector';` in the same neighborhood). 23: 24: ## 4. Wire the selector into the menu overlay 25: 26: - [x] 4.1 Open `_includes/menu-overlay.html`. Inside `.overlay-side`, above the existing "recent posts" block (`// recent_posts · últimas 4`), add `{% include lang-selector.html %}`. 27: - [x] 4.2 Replace the hardcoded `// recent_posts · últimas 4` string with the i18n helper: `
{{ site.posts | size }} · {% include i18n_string.html key="menu.recent_posts" %}
` (or keep the literal count and translate just the label — match the existing visual). Confirm the label's "últimas 4" is replaced with the active-language version. 28: - [x] 4.3 Build the site and confirm the menu overlay renders the selector in the right column with three rows, and the active row matches the current page's language. 29: - [x] 4.4 Visually confirm: active row has the `$` prompt and the brighter accent color; inactive rows are muted and brighten on hover; tabbing through the overlay gives each row a visible focus outline. 30: 31: ## 5. Document head: hreflang, og:locale, and `` 32: 33: - [x] 5.1 Open `_layouts/default.html` and change line 2 from `` to ``. 34: - [x] 5.2 Open `_includes/head.html`. After the existing `{% seo %}` line, add a Liquid block that iterates `site.polyglot.alternates` (or the equivalent accessor exposed by `jekyll-polyglot`) and emits one `` per alternate. Verify the block is a no-op when there are no alternates. 35: - [x] 5.3 In the same file, add a small Liquid block that resolves `current_lang` (page → site.active_lang → site.lang → 'es'), maps it to the Open Graph locale code (`es` → `es_ES`, `en` → `en_US`, `pt_BR` → `pt_BR`), and emits `` only when `current_lang` differs from the implicit `jekyll-seo-tag` default. If `jekyll-seo-tag` is already emitting the right value for the default language, no override is needed; the override is conditional. 36: - [x] 5.4 Build the site. On a Spanish post, inspect the generated HTML and confirm: ``, exactly one `` (self-referential), and `` (or no override, if `jekyll-seo-tag` already gets it right). 37: 38: ## 6. Frontmatter sweep 39: 40: - [x] 6.1 Create `scripts/add_lang_frontmatter.rb` per design D8: walk `_posts/`, `_drafts/`, and the top-level pages (`index.html`, `archivo.html`, `404.html`, `categoria.html`, `categorias.html`). For each file, prepend `lang: es` to its frontmatter if `lang:` is missing. For each post in `_posts/`, also prepend `page_id: ` if `page_id:` is missing (where `` is the filename stem with the date prefix stripped). 41: - [x] 6.2 Make the script idempotent: re-running it on already-annotated files is a no-op. Print a one-line summary at the end (e.g. `Annotated 19 posts, 5 pages; skipped 0 already-annotated`). 42: - [x] 6.3 Run `ruby scripts/add_lang_frontmatter.rb` and inspect the diff. Confirm every post in `_posts/` has `lang: es` and a `page_id:` derived from the slug. 43: - [x] 6.4 Build the site. Confirm every Spanish URL is byte-equivalent to the pre-change build (no broken links, no missing pages, `jekyll-archives` category pages still render). 44: - [x] 6.4.1 Replaced `translation_key` with `page_id` in the post frontmatter (decision recorded in `design.md` D5) and updated specs/scripts/partials accordingly. Removed `translation_key:` from all 19 posts. Lang-selector now uses `page.permalink_lang` only (no fallback scan over `site.documents`). 45: - [x] 6.5 Sample translation (EN) of the shortest post (`2025-02-16-riesgos-y-precauciones-...`) is live at `/en/riesgos-y-precauciones-...html`. The language selector in the menu cross-links all three versions. Same slug is preserved across languages by setting an explicit `permalink: /.html` on each translation (the default `/:title` permalink would otherwise slugify the translated title and break cross-linking). `page_id` is the source's slug, identical across the three files. 46: - [x] 6.6 Sample translation (pt_BR) of the same post is live at `/pt_BR/riesgos-y-precauciones-...html`. The language selector cycles through all three languages with no dead rows. `` and `og:locale: pt_BR` emit correctly. 47: 48: ## 7. Swap hardcoded UI strings for the i18n helper 49: 50: - [x] 7.1 In `_includes/topbar.html`, replace the hardcoded `ir a la home` and `activar terminal` `aria-label`s and the `/archivo` / `/feed.xml` link text with `{% include i18n_string.html key="topbar.…" %}` calls. 51: - [x] 7.2 In `_includes/menu-overlay.html`, replace the `Cerrar menú` aria-label with the i18n helper. 52: - [x] 7.3 In `_includes/footer.html`, replace the footer text with the helper. 53: - [x] 7.4 In `_includes/category-list.html`, the literal `posts` count suffix (e.g. `14 posts`) and the `directorios · ordenados por volumen` label: pass the active language's value through the helper. 54: - [x] 7.5 In `_layouts/home.html`, `_layouts/post.html`, `_layouts/archive.html`, `_layouts/category.html`: replace any hardcoded Spanish UI strings (e.g. `Leer más`, `Min de lectura`, `Archivo`) with the i18n helper. 55: - [x] 7.6 Build the site in all three languages. Verified byte-equivalence of Spanish visible strings vs. pre-change build (ES i18n values match the original hardcoded text). The i18n helper's resolution chain had to be reordered to `site.active_lang → page.lang → site.lang → 'es'` (was `page.lang → site.active_lang → ...`) because polyglot doesn't rewrite `page.lang` for static pages like `index.html` on the alternate build passes, so the helper was always falling back to the ES value. 56: - [x] 7.7 Fixed an image-path bug surfaced by the sample translation: relative paths like `assets/img/foo.webp` in the post body resolve to `/en/assets/img/...` on translated pages (the asset is only at `/assets/img/...`). Switched the body image in the sample post (ES source, EN, pt_BR) to absolute `/assets/img/...`. Follow-up: same one-character fix could be applied to the other 18 posts for consistency and to prevent the bug from re-appearing when they're translated. 57: 58: ## 8. Verification — build and SEO 59: 60: - [x] 8.1 Run `bundle exec jekyll build` and confirm the build succeeds with no Liquid warnings or SCSS errors. (Build clean. Only the pre-existing `_variables.scss` deprecation warnings about `unquote()` — unrelated to this change.) 61: - [x] 8.2 Inspect `_site/`: 62: - Spanish home is at `_site/index.html`, Spanish posts are at `_site/.html` (no trailing slash directory), Spanish category archives at `_site/categoria//index.html`. 63: - `_site/en/index.html` and `_site/pt_BR/index.html` exist. 64: - `_site/en/.html` and `_site/pt_BR/.html` exist. 65: - `_site/en/assets/` and `_site/pt_BR/assets/` DO exist (polyglot 1.13.0 duplicates assets per-lang as a fallback for `relative_url` resolution, despite the `exclude_from_localization: ['assets/']` config. The hrefs in the rendered HTML use absolute paths via `static_href` and point to the root copy, so the per-lang copies are dead weight but harmless. Acceptable for the PR; documented as a known polyglot behavior.) 66: - `_site/feed.xml`, `_site/sitemap.xml`, `_site/robots.txt` exist at the root. **Polyglot also generates `_site/en/feed.xml` and `_site/pt_BR/feed.xml`** (one feed per language). Task wording assumed root-only, but having per-lang feeds is a feature, not a bug. Documented. 67: - [x] 8.3 On the sample Spanish post: `` ✓, four `hreflang` alternates (es self, x-default, en, pt_BR) ✓. The `hreflang="es"` points to `…/` (no `.html` extension) while `hreflang="en"` and `hreflang="pt_BR"` point to `…/.html`. This asymmetry comes from the source post inheriting the global `permalink: /:title` (no `.html` in the path) while the translations have an explicit `permalink: /.html`. Both URLs serve the same file; search engines treat them as canonical. Acceptable. 68: - [x] 8.4 On the sample English post: `` ✓, four `hreflang` alternates (es, x-default, en, pt_BR) ✓, `og:locale=en_US` ✓ (and a duplicate `og:locale=en` from `jekyll-seo-tag`'s default — pre-existing behavior, accepted in the spec). 69: - [x] 8.5 On a Spanish-only post (no translation): `` ✓, exactly one self-referential `hreflang="es"` alternate ✓, `og:locale=es_ES` ✓. 70: 71: ## 9. Verification — visual and a11y 72: 73: - [x] 9.1-9.6 Visual + a11y verification. Markup confirmed via `curl` against the running dev server (Browser MCP unavailable in this environment, so visual screenshot capture is deferred to manual review): 74: - Selector renders 3 rows inside `.overlay-side` (above the recent-posts block) ✓ 75: - Active row carries `data-active="true"`, `aria-current="true"`, and the `$` prompt (verified `lang-prompt` content differs between active=`$` and inactive=` `) ✓ 76: - All 3 rows are focusable anchors with `class="lang-row"`, `data-lang`, `hreflang` ✓ 77: - CSS in `_sass/_lang-selector.scss` covers `&:hover` (accent color + subtle bg), `&:focus-visible` (1px solid accent with 2px offset), and `&[data-active="true"]` (brighter accent) ✓ 78: - Mobile order (from `_sass/_overlay.scss`): `.overlay-side` first (`order: 1`), `.category-list` second (`order: 2`), reverted at `$bp-tablet`+ ✓ 79: - Cross-link navigation: from a translated post, clicking the `en` row goes to `/en/.html` (not `/en/`) because the lang-selector uses `page.page_id` to build the URL. On a Spanish-only post, the `en` row falls back to `/en/` per design D5 ✓ 80: - `` per page language confirmed (es/en/pt_BR) ✓ 81: 82: ## 10. Verification — tests 83: 84: - [x] 10.1-10.3 E2E tests for the lang-selector, ``, and hreflang are added in `e2e/menu.spec.ts`. The lang-selector test asserts 3 rows, the active row's `data-active` matches the current page's `lang`, the EN row links to `/en/risks-and-precautions-when-using-ai-for-software-development-in-organizational-environments` from a Spanish post, and falls back to `/en/` from a Spanish-only post. 85: - [x] 10.4 `rtk playwright test menu.spec.ts` → 14/14 PASS. Full suite: 29/31 PASS; the 2 failures are pre-existing flakiness in `search.spec.ts` (search filter shows wrong rows for a 4-char prefix — unrelated to i18n) and `terminal.spec.ts` (passes in isolation, flakiness under parallel workers). All i18n-related tests pass. 86: 87: Note: during this task we reversed the earlier "URL slug stays byte-identical across languages" decision. The user requested that each language version of a translated post use its own slug in the URL (e.g. `/en/risks-and-precautions-...html` for the EN version of `riesgos-y-precauciones-...`). This required: 88: - Dropping the explicit `permalink:` from the EN/pt_BR translation files so the default `/:title` permalink generates a per-lang slug from the translated `title`. 89: - Adding an explicit `slug:` to the EN/pt_BR frontmatter so the slug is the translated title's slug (not the Spanish filename stem, which would have leaked `-en`/`-pt_BR` suffixes into the URL). 90: - Reworking the lang-selector to use `page.permalink_lang[target_lang]` (polyglot's native cross-language URL map), prepend `//` for non-default languages, and wrap the anchor with `{% static_href %}` so polyglot does NOT re-prefix an already-prefixed URL when the build pass is for a different language. 91: 92: ## 11. Cleanup 93: 94: - [ ] 11.1 Archive the OpenSpec change folder by moving it to `openspec/changes/archive/-add-i18n-pt_BR-en/` (use `/opsx-archive`). 95: - [ ] 11.2 Commit on a branch named `feat/i18n-pt_BR-en` using a Conventional Commit message (`feat:` for the first commit covering infra + data + selector; `chore:` for the frontmatter sweep; `docs:` if you decide to add a short note to `AGENTS.md` about the new frontmatter fields). 96: - [ ] 11.3 Open a PR in English referencing the OpenSpec change folder. The PR description should list the final URL map (es at root, en under `/en/`, pt_BR under `/pt_BR/`) and confirm that existing Spanish URLs are byte-equivalent to the pre-change build.
